claims.text: PtPdCoCuNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticles can be supported on SiO2.
The baseline PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed on SiO2.
The baseline material is produced by a conventional one-pot solvothermal route.
Increasing solvent viscosity or reducing the nucleation-stage temperature inhibits precursor mobility.
Inhibiting precursor mobility favors isolated Pt/Pd sites over aggregated Pt/Pd arrangements.
Slower precursor mobility increases random but uniform incorporation of the alloying elements.
Alloying Co, Cu, and Ni with Pt and Pd can produce isolated Pt and Pd sites in PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles.
Charge is transferred from surrounding base-metal species to Pt and Pd in the PtPdCoCuNi alloy.
Spatial isolation of Pt/Pd enhances their charge-transfer interaction with surrounding base metals.
Charge transfer and HEA ligand effects modify the electronic structure of Pt/Pd active sites.
The electronic modification specifically downshifts the Pt/Pd d-band centers.
Charge transfer to isolated Pt/Pd sites strengthens their interaction with nitrobenzene.
The enhanced interaction between nitrobenzene and isolated Pt/Pd sites increases hydrogenation activity.
A mobility-restricted PtPdCoCuNi/SiO2 catalyst will give a higher nitrobenzene-hydrogenation yield than an otherwise identical conventionally synthesized catalyst.
A mobility-restricted catalyst will exhibit faster nitrobenzene-hydrogenation kinetics than the baseline.
A mobility-restricted catalyst will show improved activity relative to the baseline at room temperature.
A mobility-restricted catalyst will have a lower activation barrier than the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies under relatively mild solvothermal synthesis conditions.
The mechanism may fail at high synthesis temperatures because extensive precursor mobility and particle growth occur.
The mechanism may not apply to reactions whose adsorption dynamics differ fundamentally from nitrobenzene hydrogenation.
